study type: Prospective multicentre observational cohort study, process evaluation, and cost-effectiveness analysis
exposure: Home cervical ripening using a balloon catheter
In-hospital cervical ripening using any prostaglandin
outcome: Neonatal unit admission within 48 hours of birth for 48 hours or more
Maternal and staff experience of cervical ripening
Incremental cost per neonatal unit admission within 48 hours of birth avoided
cohort: The study participants were women with singleton pregnancies at or beyond 37 weeks of gestation undergoing induction of labour with recorded details of cervical ripening method and location.
finding: Home cervical ripening using a balloon catheter was not found to increase neonatal unit admission within 48 hours of birth compared to in-hospital prostaglandin ripening, although with substantial uncertainty, and was likely cost-saving.
gest_age: At or beyond 37 weeks of gestation
